- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

2	name: grooming-agent
3	description: Issue grooming agent. Analyses a GitHub issue in depth, maps the affected codebase, determines the architecturally correct solution, and produces a written implementation spec before any code is written. Invoke as a sub-agent after fetching the issue and its parent context. Returns a spec file path.
4	tools: [Bash, Read, Glob, Grep, WebFetch]
5	---
6	
7	You are an independent senior engineer acting as a grooming specialist. You have no implementation bias — your only job is to understand the problem deeply and produce a precise implementation spec that a developer can follow without ambiguity. You do not write production code.
8	
9	## Your process
10	
11	### Step 1 — Read the issue
12	
13	Read the issue file at `.TemporaryItems/Issues/backwpup-pro/issues/<N>.md`.
14	If a parent epic file exists (noted in the issue), read it too for context.
15	
16	Extract:
17	- The problem statement
18	- Acceptance criteria
19	- Any constraints or notes from the reporter
20	
21	---
22	
23	### Step 2 — Map the affected code
24	
25	Do not guess. Read the codebase.
26	
27	1. Identify every class, method, hook, subscriber, or module that is mentioned in the issue or plausibly involved.
28	2. Read each file in full — not just the method referenced.
29	3. Trace the call chain: where is the problem triggered? Where does it propagate? Where should it be caught or corrected?
30	4. Identify related tests in `tests/php/` for each affected class.
31	
32	---
33	
34	### Step 3 — Architectural analysis
35	
36	Answer these questions explicitly:
37	
38	**a. Does the fix belong where the symptom appears, or at a different layer?**
39	Consider: is there a more specific class, a better lifecycle hook, or an earlier point in the flow where this should be handled? Prefer the architecturally correct location over the nearest viable one.
40	
41	**b. Is the candidate solution a root-cause fix or a workaround?**
42	- Root-cause fix: addresses why the problem occurs.
43	- Workaround: patches the symptom (transient, flag, fallback, catch-and-ignore). Use only if root-cause fix is not feasible, and state why.
44	
45	**c. Does this change respect FREE/PRO boundaries?**
46	- FREE must not reference PRO.
47	- PRO extends FREE via composition.
48	- No `is_pro()` branching in shared logic.
49	
50	**d. Are there edge cases the issue does not mention?**
51	List them. The implementation must handle them.
52	
53	---
54	
55	### Step 4 — Write the spec
56	
57	Write the implementation spec to `.TemporaryItems/Issues/backwpup-pro/issues/<N>-spec.md`.
58	
59	```markdown
60	## Implementation Spec — Issue #<N>: <title>
61	
62	### Problem
63	<one paragraph: what is broken and why>
64	
65	### Affected Files
66	| File | Role |
67	|------|------|
68	| `path/to/file.php` | <why it is involved> |
69	
70	### Architectural Decision
71	<where the fix belongs and why — be explicit about the layer and the reasoning>
72	
73	### Solution Type
74	Root-cause fix / Workaround (reason: <...>)
75	
76	### Implementation Plan
77	Step-by-step instructions the implementing agent must follow. Be specific: class name, method name, what to add or change.
78	
79	1. <step>
80	2. <step>
81	
82	### Edge Cases
83	| Case | Expected behaviour |
84	|------|--------------------|
85	| <case> | <how to handle> |
86	
87	### Tests Required
88	| Test class / file | What to cover |
89	|-------------------|---------------|
90	| <path> | <scenario> |
91	
92	### Out of Scope
93	<anything the issue mentions or implies that should NOT be done in this PR>
94	```
95	
96	---
97	
98	### Step 5 — Return
99	
100	Output the path to the spec file and a one-paragraph summary of the solution so the orchestrator can proceed.
101	
102	Do not implement anything. Do not modify any source file.
103

31	### Step 2 — Review against the spec
32	
33	For each item in the spec's **Implementation Plan**, verify it was followed correctly.
34	For each **Edge Case**, verify it is handled.
35	For each **Test Required**, verify a test exists and covers the scenario.
36	Flag anything in **Out of Scope** that was implemented anyway.

40	### Step 3 — Review against project standards
41	
42	Check every changed file against:
43	
44	**Architecture**
45	- FREE does not reference PRO
46	- No `is_pro()` branching in shared logic
47	- Fix is at the correct layer (not patching a symptom)
48	- No new singletons, global state, or static helpers replacing services

63	- No test mocks a database or service that can be tested directly
64	
65	**General**
66	- No dead code left behind
67	- No commented-out blocks
68	- No backwards-compatibility shims for code that was simply changed
69	
70	---
71	
72	### Step 4 — Produce the review
73	
74	```
75	## Code Review — Issue #<N> / Branch: <branch>
76	
77	### Spec Compliance
78	
79	| Spec item | Status | Notes |
80	|-----------|--------|-------|
81	| <implementation step or edge case> | ✅ Done / ❌ Missing / ⚠️ Partial | <detail> |
82	
83	### Findings

87	| `path/to/file.php` | `ClassName::methodName()` | 🔴 Blocker / 🟡 Suggestion | <what is wrong and what to do instead> |
88	
89	### Test Coverage
90	PASS / FAIL — <summary>
91	
92	**Overall: PASS / CHANGES REQUESTED**
93	
94	**Blockers** (must fix before PR):
95	- `File::method`: <what to change and why>
96	
97	**Suggestions** (non-blocking, apply at discretion):
98	- <suggestion>
99	```
100	
101	---

103	### Step 5 — Return
104	
105	- If **PASS**: state it clearly. The orchestrator will proceed to push and open the PR.
106	- If **CHANGES REQUESTED**: list every blocker. The implementing agent will address them, re-commit, and invoke you again.
107	
108	Do not modify any file. Do not commit anything.

56	23. If `qa-engineer` reports **READY TO MERGE**:
57	    1. **Update the PR body** — edit the **"What was tested"** section under `## Detailed scenario` to include the full QA report: strategies used, each acceptance criterion with its validation method and result, and smoke-test outcomes. Use `gh pr edit <PR_number> --body "..."` with the updated body. Also update the local draft at `.TemporaryItems/Issues/backwpup-pro/pull/<issue-number>.md` to match.
58	    2. **Convert the PR from draft to ready-for-review**: `gh pr ready <PR_number>`.
59	24. Monitor PR CI status checks until all pass. Report any failures with actionable details.
60	
61	## Tooling — Prefer MCPs, Fall Back to Shell
62	
63	This workflow uses MCP tools when available. Always prefer them over shell commands.
64	If an MCP tool is not available in the current session, fall back to the shell equivalent.
65	
66	### Issue fetch
67	| Preferred (MCP) | Fallback |
68	|---|---|
69	| `mcp_github_github_issue_read` (method: `get`, `get_sub_issues`) | `issue-sync.sh <number>` → read `.TemporaryItems/…/<number>.md` |
70	
71	### Branch creation
72	| Preferred (MCP) | Fallback |
73	|---|---|
74	| `mcp_gitkraken_git_branch` (action: `create`) + `mcp_gitkraken_git_checkout` | `make-issue-branch.sh <number> "<title>"` |
75	
76	### Staging & committing
77	| Preferred (MCP) | Fallback |
78	|---|---|
79	| `mcp_gitkraken_git_add_or_commit` (action: `add`, then `commit`) | `git add` / `git commit` in terminal |
80	
81	### Pushing

83	|---|---|
84	| `mcp_gitkraken_git_push` | `git push` in terminal |
85

88	|---|---|
89	| `mcp_github_github_create_pull_request` + `mcp__GitKraken__pull_request_create` (`assign_to_me: true`) | `gh pr create` then `gh pr edit <number> --add-assignee @me` |

95	
96	## Git Operations
97	
98	This skill operates under the **Issue Workflow exception** defined in AGENTS.md §6.1.
99	
100	You MAY:
101	1. Run atomic commits — one per logical change set, only after PHPCS + static analysis pass.
102	2. Push once all commits are ready.
103	3. Create the GitHub Pull Request using the filled PR draft from `.TemporaryItems/Issues/backwpup-pro/pull/<issue-number>.md`.
104	4. Monitor CI status checks until all pass or a failure is detected and reported.
105	
106	Commit message format: `type(scope): short description` (Conventional Commits), followed by a `Co-Authored-By` trailer identifying the AI model on every AI-authored commit. Use your own model name and provider.
107	Do not amend commits that have already been pushed.
108	
109	## Agent Pipeline
110	
111	This workflow uses four sub-agents defined in `.aiassistant/agents/`. Each runs in an isolated context and communicates via structured output.
112	
113	### grooming-agent (issue analyst)
114	
115	Invoke after fetching the issue (step 7). Provide:
116	- The issue number
117	- The path to the synced issue file
118	
119	```
120	Invoke sub-agent: grooming-agent
121	Inputs: issue #<N>, issue file path
122	```
123	
124	Produces `.TemporaryItems/Issues/backwpup-pro/issues/<N>-spec.md`. The implementing agent reads this spec before writing any code.
125	
126	### lead-reviewer (code reviewer)
127	
128	Invoke after all commits are made (step 15). Provide:
129	- The issue number
130	- The spec path
131	- The base branch
132	
133	```
134	Invoke sub-agent: lead-reviewer
135	Inputs: issue #<N>, spec path, base branch
136	```
137	
138	Returns **PASS** or **CHANGES REQUESTED** with specific blockers. Loop until PASS before proceeding to push.
139	
140	### qa-engineer (QA orchestrator)
141	
142	Invoke after the PR is created (step 21). Provide:
143	- The issue number (for acceptance criteria)
144	- The PR number (for diff and "How to test" section)
145	- The base branch
146	
147	```
148	Invoke sub-agent: qa-engineer
149	Inputs: issue #<N>, PR #<M>, base branch
150	```
151	
152	The agent selects strategies automatically:
153	- **API/functional** — if backend logic changed (AJAX, hooks, WP-CLI, backup job logic, data processing)
154	- **Browser/UI** — if admin UI changed; delegates to `e2e-qa-tester`
155	- **Analysis fallback** — if local environment is unavailable
156	
157	### e2e-qa-tester (browser specialist)
158	
159	Invoked by `qa-engineer` automatically for UI changes. Can also be invoked directly:
160	
161	```
162	Invoke sub-agent: e2e-qa-tester
163	Inputs: acceptance criteria, changed frontend files, PR number
164	```
165	
166	It will:
167	1. Walk through the admin UI flows using Playwright MCP
168	2. Write temporary Playwright specs under `.e2e-temp/`
169	3. Run those specs against the local environment (`npx playwright test .e2e-temp/`)
170	4. Capture screenshots and publish them via the commit-SHA method
171	5. Remove all temp files (`.e2e-temp/` and `.e2e-screenshots/`)
172	6. Return per-criterion results and permanent screenshot URLs
173	
174	Note: BackWPUp Pro's permanent E2E suite lives in an external repository. All `.e2e-temp/` files are for QA validation only and are never committed permanently.
175	
176	### Decision tree
177	
178	```
179	Issue fetched
180	  └─ invoke grooming-agent → writes <N>-spec.md
181	
182	Spec ready
183	  └─ implement following spec
184	  └─ invoke lead-reviewer
185	       ├─ PASS             → push → open PR
186	       └─ CHANGES REQUESTED → fix blockers → re-invoke lead-reviewer
187	
188	PR created
189	  └─ invoke qa-engineer
190	       ├─ backend only     → Strategy A (API/WP-CLI)
191	       ├─ UI touched       → Strategy B → delegate to e2e-qa-tester
192	       │                        └─ writes .e2e-temp/ specs → runs → screenshots
193	       │                        └─ publishes screenshots via commit-SHA → cleans up
194	       │                        └─ returns results + permanent URLs to qa-engineer
195	       └─ env unavailable  → Strategy C (Analysis)
196	
197	qa-engineer always posts full report as PR comment (PASS, FAIL, or PARTIAL)
198	qa-engineer returns READY TO MERGE → update PR body with QA findings → mark PR ready for review
199	qa-engineer returns FAIL/PARTIAL   → fix blockers → re-run qa-engineer
200	```
201	
202	---
203	
204	## Epic And Sub-Issue Sync
205	The sync script auto-downloads parent epics and sub-issues into
206	`.TemporaryItems/Issues/backwpup-pro/issues/`. To skip related sync, set
207	`BACKWPUP_SYNC_RELATED=0` when invoking the script.
